To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) the majority of faults that cause architectural failures are correct at the user/application level, and (2) this observation can be exploited to improve fault tolerance.
application-level correctness is more tolerant of architectural faults compared to traditional architecture-level correctness.
Application-level correctness is an effective way of improving fault tolerance in soft computations.
In summary, our research is concerned with

understanding how much more resilient applications are when defining correctness from the user's viewpoint rather than the architecture viewpoint, and exploiting the resulting enhanced error resilience to improve fault tolerance.
the impact of the application level of abstraction on fault resilience.
understanding the impact of application-level correctness on fault tolerance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
application-level correctness is more fault tolerant than architectural correctness.
application-level correctness can be a powerful and effective mechanism for enhancing fault resilience.
The extent to which programs exhibit enhanced error resilience at higher levels of correctness depends on the application.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
application-level correctness is an attractive alternative to architectural-level correctness for soft computations.
application-level correctness is a useful abstraction for fault tolerance, especially for soft computations.

we have demonstrated that the traditional notion of program correctness, which is defined in terms of the numerical integrity of the program state, is too restrictive and that a more flexible definition of correctness that is based on the application's perspective is needed to better understand the fault resilience of programs and to design effective fault tolerance mechanisms for them.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the level at which correctness is defined has a major impact on the amount of fault resilience a program exhibits.
the level of abstraction from which correctness is defined can have a significant impact on the fault tolerance of programs.
the definition of correctness has a significant impact on the fault tolerance of a program.
